decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December suggests that labor market conditions improved further even as economic growth slowed late last year.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that job conditions got better while economic growth slowed down late last year compared to the prior meeting.

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation declined further; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance, in recent months.
changes.explanation: Market measures of expected inflation dropped more, while survey-based measures remained mostly steady.

changes.quote: Given the economic outlook, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Committee chose to hold interest rates steady rather than raising them as they did previously.

changes.quote: The Committee is closely monitoring global economic and financial developments and is assessing their implications for the labor market and inflation, and for the balance of risks to the outlook.
changes.explanation: The Fed added language highlighting that it is keeping a close eye on global economic and financial market developments.

tone_quotes.quote: Given the economic outlook, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.

The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant only gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.1% APR costs about $50.42 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.02% and moved +1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.92% would rise by about $1.72 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5%, and employers added an average of 267k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 0.6% over the past year (December 2015); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -1 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.41% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future rate adjustments will be gradual and depend on incoming data regarding inflation and jobs.
